# The window-move cell-edit spec reads a cell before its rows re-render

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/workstation/WorkstationCellEditingWindowMoveNL.spec.mjs` went red three times within a day on pull requests that cannot reach it. Each time the failure was `a visible name cell is found — Received: null`, from `startCellDraft` (`:206`), in a different test:

| PR | Diff | Failing test | Shard |
|---|---|---|---|
| #21436 | `menu.List` | `:285` | e2e-engine (5/15), run 44455886438 |
| #21538 | button menus | `:442` | e2e-engine (6/15), job 135995802587 |
| #21557 | Cesium addon | `:381` | e2e-engine (13/15), job 136067346267 |

Every rerun passed. Captured as defect-notes 120e56ea and 91d174ef; the third sighting promotes it.

## The Problem

Every test starts with `setupEditableScaleGrid`, which wheels the 100k-row `scale` grid down 6000 px and waits until `scrollManager.scrollTop` and the view's DOM `scrollTop` both pass 1000. Then `startCellDraft` reads a visible `name` cell once. Scroll position is not the state that read needs: the pooled rows reach their new positions a few frames later.

Measured at `dev` `32096957fc` with a per-frame recorder started just before the wheel (headless Chromium, 4 runs per setting). DOM `scrollTop` reaches 6000 at about 25 ms. The next 2 frames (about 32 ms) hold no `name` row inside the view, and the rows are back at 57 ms. At 4× CPU throttle the gap is 3 frames (about 60 ms). Locally the settle poll returns later (about 125 ms, or 165 ms throttled), after the rows are back, so all 29 local probe runs (unthrottled, 4× and 6×) found a cell on the first read. On a loaded CI runner the render can outlast the poll's round trip, and the single read lands in the empty frames.

`popOutAndSettle` ends the same way in the popup (`scroll position holds in popup DOM and engine`). The read after it at `:328` is also single, and `:329` dereferences `postCell.recordId` before `:331` checks it.

## The Architectural Reality

- `findVisibleNameCell` (`:26`) and `findAnotherVisibleCell` (`:64`) are one-shot `evaluate` reads that return `null` when no row qualifies.
- The reads whose cell the test then uses: `:204` (asserted at `:206`), `:292` (asserted at `:294`), and `:328` and `:329` (asserted at `:331`, after the dereference).
- The same file already waits on render state with `expect.poll` elsewhere (the plugin install, both scroll settles).
- Design authority: n/a. No engine behavior is called wrong: pooled rows rendering a few frames after the scroll event is how the grid works. The defect is the test's read.

## The Fix

In the spec only: add one helper that polls a finder until it returns a cell, failing with a message that names the read, and route the four reads through it. The two finders stay one-shot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: Each of the four reads waits until its cell exists, and a timeout fails with a message naming that read (the opener reads keep their existing messages; the popup pair, which shared one combined check, gets one message each).
- [ ] AC-2: A probe that reads in the gap (straight after a `scrollTop` jump) gets `null` from the one-shot read on `dev`, and a cell from the new helper.
- [ ] AC-3: The spec passes 5 of 5 locally, and its CI shard is green.

## Out of Scope

- A different, local-only symptom of the same spec: `util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-textfield-1` during the landed pane's repaint (defect-note 64c2ad6e).
- One-shot reads after a scroll in other specs.
